main.full_text: Visia Hawelynnwas a repeat duringViolet Sorrengail's second year and a member of theRiders Quadrant.
paragraphs: Visia Hawelynnwas a repeat duringViolet Sorrengail's second year and a member of theRiders Quadrant.

Biography.full_text: Visia entered the Riders Quadrant in the same year as Violet. She nearly did not survive her first year, having angered an Orange Daggertail duringThreshing. The angereddragonleft her behind with a permanent burn scar on her face. She stayed unbonded because of this during her first year and returned for another try the next year.Visia's family was killed in the Sumerton raid her first year in the quadrant. During her second year, she was a member ofFourth Wing, Flame Section, Second Squad, the same squad as Violet,Rhiannon Matthias,Sawyer Henrick,Ridoc Gamlyn,Imogen Cardulo,Nadine,Aaric Graycastle,Sloane Mairiand more first and third years are in.During her second Threshing, she bonded a brown daggertail.She later went together with all members of her squad toAretiaand trained there. Visia and her squad were assigned to the drift that includesCatriona Cordella, when the gryphons and their fliers hiked the Medaro Pass to get to Aretia. Visia was in a group together with fellow squad member Ridoc, the flierLuellaand the latter's gryphonCibbelair. When they had to jump over a trap on the pass route, Visia made the jump easily. The flier Luella on the other side was not strong enough to make the jump, she jumped against Violet, who then fell against Visia and all together came close to the edge of the cliff. Violet was able to hold on, but Visia and Luella fell over it. They both managed to hold onto Violet's hand. When Cibbelair tried to rescue his flier, Visia was in his way, so he pulled her up first. But he could not reach Luella in time to prevent her fall.This incident involving Visia was one of the reasons for Violet's and Cat's bad relationship, because Cat blamed Violet for Luella's death. Early Life.full_text: Born inMarch, 611 AU, to the heir of TyrrendorFen Riorson, andTalia Riorson. Xaden grew up inRiorson Houselocated aboveAretia, the capital of Tyrrendor. His mother left them when he was ten, having fulfilled the requirements of her marriage contract with his father. His family carries the royal lineage of ruling the province of Tyrrendor, thus technically making Xaden the heir to the Tyrrish throne if the province had succeeded fromNavarreduring theTyrrish Rebellion. To further strengthen this royal claim prior to the beginning of the rebellion, Fen Riorson secured an alliance withViscount Tecarus, by using Xaden's royalty in a betrothal contract toCatriona Cordella, third in line for thePoromishthrone. On July 1, 627 AU, 16 year old Xaden was forced to witness the "CalldyrExecutions" of the rebellion's leadership alongside the other 107 separatist children by GeneralMelgren's dragonCodagh. When Codagh's dragonfire burned the 107 children's parents, his fire activated therune-stones each child held in their hand. These complex rune-tempered stones, created byColonel Mairi, were meant to protect the children in the event that the Rebellion failed and their parents were killed. With their activation during the executions, the runes createdrebellion relicsalong whichever arm the child was using to hold the stone in addition to protecting the children from General Melgren'ssignet. Xaden, as the oldest of the separatist children, later struck a deal withGeneral Lilith Sorrengailin which he took personal responsibility for the 107 children and in doing so received 107 scars across his back, an archaic Tyrrish custom. In return, he and the children would be allowed to fight for their lives in the Riders Quadrant instead of being executed. In the aftermath of the Rebellion, Xaden was sent to Tirvainne, along withLiam Mairi, to be fostered by Duke Lindell. While being fostered, Xaden taught Liam how to fight in order to prepare them forBasgiath. In July 631 AU, after his twentieth birthday, Xaden was conscripted and entered the Riders Quadrant alongside his best friendGarrick Tavis. The two began to meet in secret along with other unnamed "marked ones" to ensure their survival within thequadrant. During theirThreshingXaden defended his best friend fromKing Tauri'ssecond sonAlic, inevitably killing Alic. During this Threshing, Xaden bonded withSgaeyl. It was after Threshing that Xaden and Garrick decided to begin smuggling weaponry out of Basgiath in an effort to protect fliers they had partnered with againstvenin. They also began working to rebuild Aretia and Riorson House.

Fourth Wing.full_text: Xaden is present as Wingleader of Fourth Wing whenViolet Sorrengailarrives to crossthe Parapet. When assignments are being given out, Xaden uses his position to move her squad, Second Squad, Flame Section, to his Wing. This places her under his chain of command. A few weeks into the year, Xaden brings a group of first-year "marked ones" out to the woods near the river, to check in with them. He assignsImogen Carduloand Garrick Tavis to train the first-years before waving them off, and then speaks to Violet, who had been hiding in a tree above them during their meeting. They agree that he will owe her if she keeps their secret. A few weeks later in the sparring gym, Xaden forces Violet to spar against him using the opportunity to test her fighting abilities while ensuring that she still kept their meeting secret. He gradually disarms her and also offers her insights into how best to use her small stature as an advantage. He also tells her that she can't continue to rely on poisoning her opponents and that she needs to get stronger instead. Xaden gives Violet advice about how to pass the chimney obstacle onthe Gauntlet. Then he helps her again during Threshing, when Violet rushes to defend a gold feathertail, her future dragon,Andarna. As per theCodex, Xaden was barred from interfering, but he found a loophole by having his dragon Sgaeyl call hermateTairnto come help Violet defend Andarna. When Tairn bonds with Violet, it ties Violet's life to Xaden's through their dragons bond. When Xaden discovers Violet has trouble staying on her dragon, he crafts a rider's saddle for Tairn so Violet would be safe flying and fighting seated (and tied) to Tairn's back. At the end of the year, for the final War Games, Xaden chooses Violet to join his riot which was made up exclusively of marked ones.Dain Aetos'sfather,Colonel Aetos, assigns Xadens riot toAthebynewhich is outside of thewards. Upon arriving at Athebyne, they discover the outpost has been abandoned. There are new orders saying that the group can either stay and help protectRessonfrom venin andwyvern, or they can relocate to another outpost. The group decides to fight in theBattle of Ressonand Liam andSoleildie in the battle. Violet gets poisoned and Xaden brings her to Aretia in a panic. Its there that it's revealed that her brotherBrennanis still alive as he mends her and Violet recovers in a coma for three days.

Iron Flame.full_text: After being missing for six days while they stayed in Aretia withthe Revolution,Xaden, Violet, and the surviving members of the war games riot return to Basgiath. They arrive just as Xaden is about to be announced as the first cadet on thedeath rollbyCaptain Fitzgibbons.Colonel Aetosis convinced that Xaden is lying about the gryphon attack, but Violets mother, General Lilith Sorrengail, dismisses Aetos after questioning her daughter about their absence. It's during this formation that Xaden graduates from Basgiath and is assigned to the eastern wing atSamara'soutpostknown for being the front line of the war against Poromiel. He and Violet begin to exchange letters as they spend weeks apart because Violet is forced to remain behind for her second year at Basgiath. WhenMajor Varrishkidnaps and imprisons Violet for 4 days after theArchiveHeist, Xaden sacrifices the secrecy of the revolution by dropping wyvern carcasses along theNavarrianborder before flying to Basgiath to rescue her. It's during this rescue that he, Violet, and Dain convince half the riders quadrant, along with a fewscribes, to side with the revolution by exposing the truth about the war and the existence of Venin. Xaden, as the heir of Aretia and therefore Tyrrendor, is part of the council (nicknamedThe Assembly) that rulesthe Revolution. After a meeting with Viscount Tecarus, the assembly agrees to accept the survivinggryphonfliersfromCliffsbane Flight Academywhen Zolya is taken over by venin. After getting word thatGeneral Melgrenwants to meet, he goes and speaks to him to find out that Navarre needs assistance or they will all be slaughtered. Xaden refuses until the last second, alongside agreement from the Assembly to only guard the wardstone chamber inside Basgiath. He leads the battle against the wyvern and venin, eventually ending up alone withthe Sageexperiencing burnout until he turns venin in an attempt to stay alive and save Violet, who is also experiencing burnout during the battle.

Violet Sorrengail.full_text: For more insight on their relationship please check out theRiorgail page. You know why you're still alive? Because you're the scale I currently judge myself against every night. Every day I let you live, I get to convince myself that there's still a part of me that's a decent person. So if you want to quit, then please, spare me the temptation and fucking quit. But if you want to do something, then do it. Xaden to Violet,Fourth Wing, Chapter 10 Xaden to Violet,Fourth Wing, Chapter 10 Violet and Xaden byillustratinghan Xaden and Violet share a complicated history, starting with their families' involvement in the Tyrrish Rebellion. Xaden's father, Fen Riorson was the head of the rebellion and accused of killing Violet's older brother Brennan Sorrengail, thus leading Violet's mother General Lilith Sorrengail to hunt Fen down, capture, and execute him. Lilith Sorrengail was later also responsible for placing the 107 scars on Xaden's back when he took responsibility for the 107 separatist children by claiming through an archaic tyrrish custom. Due to this shared history, Violet was convinced upon entering the Riders Quadrant that Xaden was out to kill her in retribution. However, when she fails to report his secret meetings, Xaden begins to take an interest in her, which culminated in a moment during Threshing when Xaden and Sgaeyl intervened on Violet's behalf to protect her fromJack,Oren, andTynan, who were out to killAndarnafor being an unrideable dragon. Because Violet showed courage standing up against the three attackers on Andarna's behalf, Tairn chooses her as his rider, thus tying Violet's life to Xaden's as their dragons are a mated pair. This means that should one of them, or their dragons, suffer a fatal injury, it could result in a chain of events that leads the other rider's death. Therefore Xaden could no longer kill Violet without threatening his own life.

Xaden to Violet,Fourth Wing, Chapter 10 Xaden to Violet,Fourth Wing, Chapter 10 Violet and Xaden byillustratinghan Xaden and Violet share a complicated history, starting with their families' involvement in the Tyrrish Rebellion.

Xaden's father, Fen Riorson was the head of the rebellion and accused of killing Violet's older brother Brennan Sorrengail, thus leading Violet's mother General Lilith Sorrengail to hunt Fen down, capture, and execute him.
Lilith Sorrengail was later also responsible for placing the 107 scars on Xaden's back when he took responsibility for the 107 separatist children by claiming through an archaic tyrrish custom.
Due to this shared history, Violet was convinced upon entering the Riders Quadrant that Xaden was out to kill her in retribution.

However, when she fails to report his secret meetings, Xaden begins to take an interest in her, which culminated in a moment during Threshing when Xaden and Sgaeyl intervened on Violet's behalf to protect her fromJack,Oren, andTynan, who were out to killAndarnafor being an unrideable dragon.
Because Violet showed courage standing up against the three attackers on Andarna's behalf, Tairn chooses her as his rider, thus tying Violet's life to Xaden's as their dragons are a mated pair.
This means that should one of them, or their dragons, suffer a fatal injury, it could result in a chain of events that leads the other rider's death.
Therefore Xaden could no longer kill Violet without threatening his own life.

Early life.full_text: According toTairneanach, Andarna's parents passed before she hatched. She is looked after by Tairneanach andSgaeyl, as well as other dragon elders. Andarna waited 650 years to hatch. She waited until Violet's 18th birthday, when she heard the elders talk about the weakling daughter of their general, the girl forecasted to become the head of the scribes, and she knew Violet would have the mind of a scribe and the heart of a rider. Fourth Wing.full_text: Andarna is approximately 2 years old when she meetsViolet Sorrengailand chooses her as her rider. She will be full-grown in a year or two. During Presentation, she flew from the Vale and joined the dragons as cadets were presented. Some of the cadets saw the small Feathertail as weak and helpless, and therefore unworthy. During Threshing, Violet overheardJack Barlowe, Oren Seifert, and Tynan plotting to kill the Feathertail. She chose to defend the dragon from the group. While Violet chased off Jack, the other two wounded her, but she and Andarna were joined by Tairneanach, who incinerated Tynan. When it was time for Violet to officially announce her dragon bond, she was surprised to find that not only did Tairneanach choose her, but Andarna as well, making Violet the first rider to bond two dragons. Some time after bonding, Violet trains in flying with Tairneanach, but not Andarna, as she is too small to bear a rider. Violet is attacked while asleep by a few unbonded cadets wanting to kill her in hopes of bonding with Tairneanach, and Andarna uses her power through Violet, briefly stopping time and allowing Violet to get away asXadenarrived, killing her attackers. The two riders meet their dragons, and realize Andarna (and Feathertail dragons, in general) is not yet fully matured and thus was able to push her full powers through to Violet, without Violet developing a signet. Using the power caused Andarna to suffer exhaustion for days after the attack. Violet and Xaden promise to keep the secret between them. Andarna allows Violet to use their signet once again during the first War Games, to help Violet saveLiam Mairiin time when he falls from his dragon. Andarna has trouble keeping up with Tairneanach during long flights, so Xaden designs a saddle for her to link under Tairneanach whenever she's tired, so she can fly with him and Violet more often. During theBattle of Resson, Tairneanach and Violet command Andarna to stay hidden, as it is dangerous for her. She doesn't listen, however, and at a critical time, stops time for Violet, so she can strike a venin with her lightling. She also catches Violet when she falls from Tairneanach, saving her life. But using all that power and being away from the Vale made Andarna grow faster than she was supposed to. When Violet wakes up inAretiaafter the battle, she notices her bond to Andarna isn't golden anymore, and Xaden mentions in his chapter that she's now huge.

Iron Flame.full_text: When Violet wakes up in Aretia and finally gets to see Andarna, she finds her sleeping, and now a Black Dragon, smaller than average, but bigger than before. Tairneanach explains Andarna is now a teenager, a complicated age for dragons, and that they need to take her back to the Vale, where she needs to go into the Dreamless Sleep for a few weeks and develop. They manage to do it, but Andarna wakes up a few times during her sleep, when she shouldn't. It also takes her longer than necessary. While Andarna is in her sleep, Violet does her best to keep her hidden, refusingVice-Commandant Varrishto bring her to lessons and taking punishments for it. When Violet is captured and tortured by Varrish, Andarna remains in her Dreamless Sleep. She also sleeps once she is rescued and everyone moves to Aretia, being carried by Tairneanach the whole way there. Once in the Valley the following day, she finally awakes. She now looks like a Black Scorpiontail, although Violet notes her scales are shimmering and seem to reflect the colors around her. Andarna has trouble expanding one of her wings, and easily loses balance, and Tairneanach explains secretly to Violet that the mass expanditure of energy inRessonforced her into a rapid rate of growth, and instead of being at the Vale in Basgiath or the Valley at Aretia, she spent that day travelling. And then she was moved again, and woke up several times, making her growth unpredictable. The seconds set of muscles that's supposed to be along the front of her wings did not develop, so now she needs to strengthen the existing muscle to compensate and be able to fly, however, she won't ever be able to bear a rider. Andarna remains a teenager throughout the rest of the book, constantly making snarky comments at Violet and Tairneanach, and not listening to them. She also keeps on growing size. She is there to help Violet when she,SloaneandCatget trapped into a cave withSolas. Andarna goes to Violet's rescue, and ends up killing Solas. She is then questioned by the elders, who find her actions justifiable, but Tairneanach explains to Violet that to slay another dragon is a heavy mark upon the soul, even when in defense of yourself or your rider. Near the end of the book, when everyone is back in Basgiath for the final battle,Jesiniafinishes translating Lyra's Journal, and Violet realizes the truth, and asks Andarna about it. It is revealed she is not a Black dragon at all, but a 7th breed, whose scales change color. She explains to Violet only the elders know about it, and that she hadn't told her because if she couldn't figure it out by herself, she wasn't worthy of knowing. Andarna then confesses she waited 650 years to hatch, until Violet's 18th birthday, when she heard the elders talk about the weakling daughter of their general, the girl forecasted to become the head of the scribes, and she knew Violet would have the mind of a scribe and the heart of a rider. She knew then Violet would be hers. Andarna was left behind by her breed to breathe fire for the wardstone, from what she can remember.

Onyx Storm.full_text: In Onyx Storm, Andarna seems to have matured her behavior, and is now more composed and adult-like. She seems to be closer to Violet than the last two books. At the start of the book, in the prologue, Andarna speaks in Violet's mind, promising her that they together will find a cure for Xaden, and also find her kind. She cooperated with her rider in order to make requests for the Senarium about the expedition to look for the seventh breed. She gives Violet the second signet: Dreamwalker, a form of inntinnsic. Throughout the book Andarna supports Violet, until they find the irid dragons and one of them, Leothan, asks her to come with him, so that she could be taught the ways of the seventh breed. At this point she finds herself struggling between her loyalty to her rider, and her wish to finally see her den and live with her fellow dragon kind. Violet encourages her to go, despite the sadness, and so Andarna breaks their bond and flies away with the older Iridescent dragon, much to Sgaeyl's astonishment and anger. However, by the end of the book, she returns to her rider in order to fight with and protect her.

She gives Violet the second signet: Dreamwalker, a form of inntinnsic.

At this point she finds herself struggling between her loyalty to her rider, and her wish to finally see her den and live with her fellow dragon kind.
Violet encourages her to go, despite the sadness, and so Andarna breaks their bond and flies away with the older Iridescent dragon, much to Sgaeyl's astonishment and anger.
However, by the end of the book, she returns to her rider in order to fight with and protect her.

Physical Description.full_text: Andarna is a Gold Feathertail. She is missing her dragon claws and is just about large enough in size to carry Violet. Her voice in Violet's mind is described as high and sweet. After waking up from her Dreamless Sleep, she develops a Scorpiontail. She can now change the color of her scales, a trait only attributed tothe Seventh Breed, though she disguises as a black dragon. She is missing the second set of muscles along the fronts of her wings that form during the growth process, impacting her ability to fly for long periods as well as bear a rider.

Violet Sorrengail.full_text: Andarna is affectionate towards Violet, often showing her support while Tairneanach acts pessimistic. She is shown to care a lot about her rider, even giving her the gift of stopping time, despite it consuming all her energy. She joined the adult dragons in the journey to Athebyne, and ultimately took part in battle against the Venins, suggesting Violet to use her gift to stop the creatures, despite knowing it would take all her energy. After Threshing, Violet remarks to the golden dragon that she could have flown away when attacked by Barlowe and his friends. The feathertail simply answers that she wanted to help, despite not having claws, nor being able to spit fire.

The black swordtail is seen not too far from Melgren, among the trees. After general Melgren's meeting with Aretia's forces doesn't go as he planned, Codagh leans closer to the ground and insures Melgren's safety, with general's back turned to Xaden and his allies. Afterwards he's flown to Samara, where Melgren prepares for a loosing battle. However, due to Melgren not being able to use his signet on children of rebellious leaders, he does not see the battle against venin in the skies above Basgiath. The forces hold off venin until Melgren is able to fly in on Codagh's back from Samara. When Codagh arrives at the war college with his rider, Violet convinces him to talk to her. Early Life.full_text: He is the child of Murtcuideam and Fiaclanfuil and descended from the cunning Dubhmadinn line. He's a little over a hundred years old, which makes him about middle aged. He's revered as a battle dragon amongDragonkind, and is accredited for the defeat of theTyrrish Rebelliondespite nearly dying during theBattle of Aretiawhen his only other previous riderNaolinburned out savingBrennan Sorrengail. Because of his rare color and breed of tail, Tairn is also considered one of the deadliest dragons in Navarre. Prior to the events ofFourth Wing, Tairn had refused to bond in the five years between Naolin's death and Violet's Threshing.

Fourth Wing.full_text: Tairn first appears during Threshing, despite not having planned to as he was not present for Presentation. He flew in to protectAndarnafromTynan,Jack BarloweandOren Seifert. Due to Violets bravery for going against three cadets to protect a feathertail, Tairn chose to bond with her. Other than that, he also chose her because of her intelligence. Due to Violet's injuries while protecting Andarna, Tairn accommodates Violet mounting him by angling his leg into a ramp for her. When Violet falls off as they took flight, Tairn surprised her by catching her repeatedly. He even uses his own magic to hold Violet into place. After Andarna decides to bond with Violet too, the Empyrean decides what to do. He orders Violet to stay close to Xaden for protection. He knows other unbonded cadets will try to attack her, hoping that Tairn might bond them once Violet is out of the picture. Eventually, it is decided that Violet can keep both dragons, so Tairn gives her a black relic of a dragon across her back. During the first flight lesson, Tairn decides to fly second, only behind Professor Kaoris dragon. He allows Violet to fall countless times, but also catches her every single time. Future flight lessons go similarly, with Violet falling becoming less frequent even with Tairn doing all sorts of tricks in the air. A few nights later, Tairn wakes Violet up while seven other cadets attempt to murder her in her sleep. He warns Xaden who arrives in time to save her from the murder attempt. After Montserrat, Tairn begins wearing a saddle that Xaden designed based on Tairn's demands and specifications to help Violet keep her seat. Before arriving at Athebyne, it is revealed that Tairn did not tell Violet about the Venin due to a promise he made to his mate, Sgaeyl. Once they reach Athebyne and the true mission for the War Games is revealed, Tairn is eager to fulfill the role of general to the riot of dragons and drift of gryphons defendingResson.

Physical Description.full_text: Tairn is a Black Morningstartail with scarred black wings and one of the biggest dragons Violet has ever seen, who doesn't even come close to reaching his ankle. His underbelly is covered in rock-hard scales and he has long claws. His scales are larger and thicker than Violet's hand. He has a series of pointed spikes that ripple down most of his neck like a mane. His seat is a smooth, scaly divot just in front of his wings. The pommel is a thick ridge of scales where his neck meets his shoulders. With Violet, he wears a saddle made out of sumptuous black leather, completed with two raised pommels for her hands and stirrups, including a belt and thigh straps.

Physical Description.full_text: The Sage, later known as Berwyn, has a gaunt face, sharp cheekbones, thin lips, and rivers of red veins fanning in every direction around his soulless eyes. His eyes are dark and eyelash-less. While usually hooded, there is a glimpse of white scalp under his slicked-back, thinning hair. Shadows mark the gaunt hallows of his cheekbones on an eerily youthful face, and his lips are cracked and dry. Red-rimmed eyes, distended veins spiderwebbing across his temples and cheeks. Tanned arms and gnarled, bony hands and fingers. Wears a hooded floor length robes that many high-level venin wear and carries a staff. The floor length robe is purple at the Battle of Resson, blue at Basgiath, and various colors in the nightmares (including maroon). In the Battle of Resson the staff is described as a long red cane made from misshapen wood.

Physical Description.full_text: Theophanie has long silver hair, seen in a braid. She has eerie red eyes with scarlet-red veins on her temples beside her eyes, Violet says it reminds her of a masquerade mask as she also has a faded tattoo on her forehead. The faded tattoo is the emblem of Dunne, two crossed swords gripped in the center by a claw. The red glow around her irises is about ten shades brighter than those on Jack. She has high cheekbones, a full mouth, and would be stunningly beautiful if not for the venin features and her skin is eerily pale. She often wears the robes Sages are often seen wearing, notably a gauzy purple robe.Also seen wearing a scarlet long-sleeved tunic and pants. Theophanie has gnarled fingers.

Storm-Wielding.full_text: Initially, it is presumed that Theophanie is a lightning-wielder because there is lightning during the time she appears. However, Theophanie is actually a powerful storm wielder, more powerful than General Sorrengail. She is so powerful she is able to create tornados a feat that General Sorrengail had never accomplished. Storm wielding can alter temperature and other elements weatherand wield the power of storms. Weather is the one great equalizer in battle, equally detrimental or favorable to both sides given the conditions. Without our wielders swaying that element to our advantage, we are at its mercy. Tactics, A Modern Guide to Aerial Combat by Marjor Constance Cara

Iron Flame.full_text: After being crushed by the weight of a mountain and presumed dead, Jack is mended byNolonover the course of several months in secret. His dragon,Baide, keeps his survival a secret fromthe EmpyreanuntilProfessor Markhamreintroduces him to the quadrant. Later on Jack rushes to the turret during his watch after hearing screams. He saves Violet from an assassination attempt by piercing theinfantrysoldier's throat and pulling her up from the edge. Violet is confused and questions Jack about why he did not take the chance to throw her off the tower and kill her. He explains that he has changed after nearly dying and receiving a second chance in life, which makes both of them even after Violet almost killed him. He leaves the tower without further notice. In thewardstonechamber during the battle of Basgiath, he is seen riding Baide for the last time before grabbing her by her horns and pushing a dagger in between the hard scales that protect her neck. Baide ends up falling onto the wardstone before bleeding out, extinguishing the flame on top. However, Jack does not die, as it is revealed that he turned venin prior to her death. Jack stays locked up in a cell after he destroyed the ward stone. He is visited by Xaden, who asks for a cure. Jack informs him that he now considers him a brother and that they don't need to be cured.

Onyx Storm.full_text: Violet, having heard Xaden's conversation with Jack, getsImogento wipe Jack's memory of the encounter.Soon after the battle of Basgiath, a group of venin attempt to break Jack out of his cell. One of the venin that comes to retrieve him isTheophanie. The mission fails and he remains in holding. Jack is questioned numerous times by Nolon and Markham, offering no information. Violet begins secretly interrogating him herself, with the help of Imogen's memory erasure signet. He is offered a quick death via oranges or to drain from a piece ofalloyand stay awake for another week. He chooses the alloy and reveals and in return must answer her questions. He reveals that initiates and asims can be sensed by other venin and that non-bonded people must be taught how to pull from the source. Theophanie tries again to get to Jack by capturingMira.Garrickretrieves Jack using the Rybestad chest to contain him.When Theophanie lays eyes on Jack, she throws a dagger at him. The dagger misses, and Garrick secured Jack in the chest and takes him away from danger using his distance wielding. Xaden notes that the reason Theophanie would want him dead is because Jack knows important intel.

Personality.full_text: Jack is cocky and impatient. He feels no remorse for tossing other cadets off the parapet into their death and tried on multiple occassions to kill Violet. His aggressive and envious behavior towards others was in alignment with his dragon Baide, who is stated to be aggressive. Jack firmly believes in the idea that those lacking strength have no place in the Riders Quadrant, whether they behumansor dragons. This is why he attempted to killAndarnaduringThreshing, assuming her small size made her as vulnerable as Violet. "Even his voice reeks of arrogance."

Violet Sorrengail.full_text: Since conscription day, Jack has had a strong hatred for Violet. He attempts to kill her several times over the course of their first year. In his own words he see's Violet as frail and weak, and targeted her after she managed to bond Tairn who he had his sights set on prior to Threshing. After surviving his presumed death, Jack makes amends by saving Violets life, though he reveals his true colors during the final battle at Basgiath by destroying the wardstone.
